about: Grand Galactic's whole design in one file. Each section is a table: one row per thing, one column per property. Edit here, then run tools/preflight.py and tools/gen.py. Not-applicable cells hold 0 or "none" on purpose.

rules.about: Global rules. Act timing, raids and moon length live in difficulties.json and moon_lengths.json.

rows.desc: Difficulty selected the first time the game runs (sheets/difficulties.json).
Moon length selected the first time the game runs (sheets/moon_lengths.json).
What every run starts with (plus 3 of the ethic's worker card). No resources: the pool in the top bar starts at 0 and fills as your Pops work.
How many worker cards (Pop or Drone) a run starts with.
A hostile card with no battle picks a fight with a nearby card this often.
A tutorial step the first moon waits for, or none (time always runs; the start has enough Food for the first moons).
Unfed Pops simply die at moon end (no corpse card).
Drop cards here to sell them for their value in Energy.
Most cards in one stack.
Names given to surveyed star systems (never repeated; once used up, names repeat with II, III...).
Most star systems you can own at once, counting your capital. Surveying is unlimited; claiming is not.
Seconds a ship takes to carry a stack one system-step across the table (diagonal steps count as one).
Tabs of the Blueprint book (Tab key). A recipe goes in the first tab with a prefix its id starts with. Every recipe is listed: known ones in full, locked ones with the technology that unlocks them.
Most warships one fleet (a stack of warships) can hold before Fleet Doctrine research.
Fleet size after each Fleet Doctrine technology is researched.
Seconds a Baby must spend on a City District to grow into a Pop.
The first moon whose end costs Food/Energy upkeep. Earlier moons live off rations, so an empty start can't starve.
No raids before this moon; after it, raiders come every raid_every_moons (difficulty) moons.
Raids before this moon are Pirates; from it, every other raid is the tougher Marauders.
A colonised planet or outpost with no Pop on it still yields, every (its yield time x this) seconds.
In an energy deficit (upkeep unpaid last moon) all work takes this percentage of its normal time.
In an energy deficit your ships deal this percentage of their damage.
Each level of a repeatable technology adds this many percent.
Rival empires in a run (picked at random from the empires sheet).
Seconds an Envoy needs at an empire's capital to raise intel by one level (about a moon).
At war, a rival empire sends a raid fleet to your capital every this many moons.
A tributary pays this percentage of its income to you each moon (as Energy and Minerals).
Species selected the first time the game runs.

difficulties.about: Difficulty levels picked on the empire screen. Multipliers apply to every hostile card (monsters, raiders, guardians, crises); the moons set when each act starts.

rows.name: Ensign
rows.desc: Relaxed. Weaker enemies, rare raids, cheaper packs and a late crisis. An extra Pop at the start.

rows.name: Captain
rows.desc: The intended balance.

rows.name: Admiral
rows.desc: Tougher enemies, frequent raids and an earlier crisis.

rows.name: Grand Admiral
rows.desc: For veterans. Frequent raids, tough enemies, and the crisis comes at moon 17.

moon_lengths.about: Moon length picked on the empire screen: real seconds per moon. Longer moons mean more time to work between feedings.

rows.name: Short
rows.desc: 60 seconds per moon. Fast and hungry.

rows.name: Standard
rows.desc: 90 seconds per moon.

rows.name: Long
rows.desc: 120 seconds per moon. More time to plan.

rows.name: Relaxed
rows.desc: 180 seconds per moon. Plenty of time between feedings.

ethics.about: The empire pick before a run. Every run also gets the shared start cards in rules.start_cards; worker_card replaces the 3 starting Pops.

rows.name: Militarist
rows.desc: Start with a Shipyard, a Corvette and Corvette tech. Free Military pack.

rows.name: Spiritualist
rows.desc: Start with a Temple and a Priest. Free Society pack.

rows.name: Materialist
rows.desc: Start with a Research Lab and a Scientist. Free Research pack.

rows.name: Machine Intelligence
rows.desc: Drones instead of Pops: no Food, but 1 Energy each per moon. Robot Assembly Plant and Robotics tech. Free Industry pack.

categories.about: Card categories. Each card is tinted by its category's colour over the Stacklands card frame.

cards.about: Every card in the game. name_loc is a Stellaris localisation key read from the player's install; name is used only if that key is missing. art is an asset_refs id. Not-applicable cells hold 0 or "none" on purpose. Cards tagged workplace are worked by Pops (recipe w_yield); cards tagged star are observed by Science Ships (recipe x_observe). Combat: damage hits shield, then armor, then hull (hp). shield_regen and hull_regen are per second; evasion is the chance to dodge a shot; slots is how many components a ship or starbase can fit; weapon names a components row whose damage profile this card's attack uses.

rows.name: Pop
rows.desc: A citizen of your empire. Stack on a district or planet to work it, or on a blueprint to research it. Eats 2 Food each moon.

rows.name: Drone
rows.desc: A machine unit. Works like a Pop but runs on 1 Energy each moon instead of Food.

rows.name: Priest
rows.desc: A Pop of faith. Works anywhere; Unity work goes 50% faster.

rows.name: Scientist
rows.desc: Leader. Researches blueprint cards twice as fast as a Pop, and studies anomalies. Get one from the Research pack, or Research Lab + Pop + 2 Research.

rows.name: Admiral
rows.desc: Leader. Drop on a fleet (a stack of warships) to take command: every ship in that fleet hits 50% harder. Fleet size is limited until Fleet Doctrine research.

rows.name: Governor
rows.desc: Leader. Districts and planets in the same stack produce 50% faster.

rows.name: Energy Credits
rows.desc: The galactic currency. Kept in your pool (top bar); click a pack to spend it.

rows.name: Minerals
rows.desc: Kept in your pool. Builds districts, ships and structures.

rows.name: Food
rows.desc: Kept in your pool. Each Pop eats 2 at the end of every moon.

rows.name: Alloys
rows.desc: Warships and starbases are made of these.

rows.name: Consumer Goods
rows.desc: Keeps a growing population happy; needed for new Pops.

rows.name: Research
rows.desc: Stack with a Scientist to discover technologies.

rows.name: Unity
rows.desc: The will of your people. Builds temples and academies.

rows.name: Influence
rows.desc: Claim new star systems with Starbases.

rows.name: Exotic Gases
rows.desc: Strategic resource. Refines into Research.

rows.name: Rare Crystals
rows.desc: Strategic resource. Refines into Alloys.

rows.name: Volatile Motes
rows.desc: Strategic resource. Fuel for terraforming.

rows.name: Zro
rows.desc: Rare psionic resource. Sell high or use in Titan research.

rows.name: Dark Matter
rows.desc: Rare resource. Needed for Titans.

rows.name: Living Metal
rows.desc: Rare resource. Repairs and armours a Battleship into a Titan hull.

rows.name: Homeworld
rows.desc: Your capital. A Pop here makes Energy. Its planetary defences shoot back at raiders. Click it to issue an Edict (2 Unity = 1 Influence). If it falls, the run is lost.

rows.name: Desert World
rows.desc: Dry and rich in ore. Colonised, its Pops mine Minerals. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Arid World
rows.desc: Sun-baked plains. Colonised, its Pops make Energy. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Savanna World
rows.desc: Grasslands. Colonised, its Pops grow Food. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Ocean World
rows.desc: A world of seas. Colonised, its Pops fish up Food fast. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Tropical World
rows.desc: Jungle world. Colonised, its Pops make Consumer Goods. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Continental World
rows.desc: Temperate and green. Colonised, its Pops grow Food. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Arctic World
rows.desc: Frozen wastes hiding old secrets. Colonised, its Pops make Research. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Tundra World
rows.desc: Cold steppe. Colonised, its Pops mine Minerals. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Alpine World
rows.desc: Mountain monasteries. Colonised, its Pops make Unity. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Tomb World
rows.desc: A nuked graveyard of a fallen people. Colonised, its ruins give Research. Can be terraformed. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster). A colony: 2 Pops + 3 Food on it raise a Baby, who grows up there.

rows.name: Gas Giant
rows.desc: Build an outpost with a Construction Ship, then siphon Exotic Gases. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster).

rows.name: Asteroid
rows.desc: Build an outpost with a Construction Ship, then mine Rare Crystals. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster).

rows.name: Barren World
rows.desc: Lifeless rock. Build an outpost, then mine Minerals. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster).

rows.name: Molten World
rows.desc: Lava seas. Build an outpost, then skim Volatile Motes. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster).

rows.name: Frozen World
rows.desc: Ice-locked. Build an outpost, then study it for Research. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster).

rows.name: Toxic World
rows.desc: Poisonous skies. Build an outpost, then tap its Energy. Once yours it also produces on its own, slowly (a Pop on it works much faster).

rows.name: Yellow Star
rows.desc: A steady yellow sun. Park a Science Ship here to study it for Research.

rows.name: Red Dwarf
rows.desc: A dim red star. A Science Ship studies it slowly for Research.

rows.name: Blue Giant
rows.desc: A huge, hot blue star. A Science Ship studies it quickly for Research.

rows.name: Black Hole
rows.desc: Nothing escapes it - except, with patience, Dark Matter. Park a Science Ship here.

rows.name: Neutron Star
rows.desc: A collapsed stellar core. A Science Ship harvests Rare Crystals from its crust.

rows.name: Pulsar

rows.name: Nebula
rows.desc: A glowing gas cloud. A Science Ship collects Exotic Gases from it.

rows.name: Generator District
rows.desc: A Pop here makes Energy.

rows.name: Mining District
rows.desc: A Pop here mines Minerals.

rows.name: Agriculture District
rows.desc: A Pop here grows Food.

rows.name: City District
rows.desc: Two Pops here (and 3 Food from your pool) raise a Baby, who grows into a Pop after 60 seconds here. Click it to train a Governor.

rows.name: Research Lab
rows.desc: A Pop here makes Research. Click it to train a Scientist instead (a Pop + 2 Research).

rows.name: Alloy Foundry
rows.desc: A Pop here smelts 2 Minerals into 2 Alloys. Click it to smelt Rare Crystals instead.

rows.name: Civilian Industries
rows.desc: A Pop here turns 2 Minerals into Consumer Goods.

rows.name: Temple
rows.desc: A Pop here makes Unity. Click it to ordain a Priest instead.

rows.name: Robot Assembly Plant

rows.name: Military Academy

rows.name: Shipyard
rows.desc: Click it to choose a ship or ship part to build; the cost comes from your pool. A damaged warship + 1 Alloy here gets repaired.

rows.name: Starbase
rows.desc: Defends its system: joins any battle on its board.

rows.name: Science Ship
rows.desc: Surveys uncharted systems, opening new boards.

rows.name: Construction Ship
rows.desc: Click it to choose what to build (districts, buildings, a Shipyard); the cost comes from your pool. Also claims systems and builds outposts.

rows.name: Colony Ship
rows.desc: Carries a Pop. Drop on a habitable planet to colonise it.

rows.name: Corvette
rows.desc: Fast, cheap warship. Stack warships into a fleet; an Admiral commands the whole fleet.

rows.name: Destroyer
rows.desc: Escort warship.

rows.name: Cruiser
rows.desc: Line warship.

rows.name: Battleship
rows.desc: Heavy warship with long-range guns.

rows.name: Titan
rows.desc: Flagship with 5 component slots and its own shields. Its aura makes every ship in the battle 25% stronger.

rows.name: Uncharted System
rows.desc: Send a Science Ship to survey it and open a new star system board.

rows.name: Guardian Signal
rows.desc: Something vast waits out here. Survey it to open a Guardian's system.

rows.name: Anomaly
rows.desc: Let a Scientist study it. Who knows what you'll find.

rows.name: Derelict Ship
rows.desc: Salvage it with a Construction Ship.

rows.name: Precursor Artifact
rows.desc: Relic of a vanished empire. Sell it, or let a Scientist decode it.

rows.name: Corvettes
rows.desc: Blueprint. Put a Pop (slow) or a Scientist (fast) on it to research it. Shipyard + 2 Alloys = Corvette.

rows.name: Destroyers

rows.name: Cruisers

rows.name: Space Amoeba
rows.desc: Drifting space life. Mostly harmless.

rows.name: Tiyanki
rows.desc: Space whale. Hunting one yields plenty of Food.

rows.name: Crystalline Entity
rows.desc: Living crystal. Shatters into Rare Crystals.

rows.name: Void Cloud
rows.desc: Energy-draining void creature.

rows.name: Mining Drone
rows.desc: Ancient automaton still strip-mining. Drops Minerals.

rows.name: Pirate Raider
rows.desc: Space pirates. They raid your boards; their wrecks hold Alloys.

rows.name: Marauder Raiders
rows.desc: Nomad warlords. Tough, and they pay out in Alloys and Influence.

rows.name: Prethoryn Swarm

rows.name: Unbidden Warform

rows.name: Contingency Drone
rows.desc: A sterilisation unit of the machine crisis.

rows.name: Ether Drake
rows.desc: An ancient dragon sleeping on a hoard. Guardian.

rows.name: Dimensional Horror

rows.name: Enigmatic Fortress
rows.desc: A fortress of unknown origin. Guardian.

rows.name: Prethoryn Queen
rows.desc: Heart of the Prethoryn Scourge. Kill her to save the galaxy.

rows.name: Unbidden Avatar

rows.name: Sentinel Core

rows.name: Crisis Rift

rows.name: Fleet Doctrine
rows.desc: Blueprint. Research it to let one fleet hold up to 6 warships.

rows.name: Advanced Fleet Doctrine

rows.name: Baby

rows.name: Industrial Farming

rows.name: Cold Fusion Power
rows.desc: Blueprint. Put a Pop (slow) or a Scientist (fast) on it to research it. Energy work is another 25% faster.

rows.name: Advanced Metallurgy

rows.desc: Blueprint. Put a Pop (slow) or a Scientist (fast) on it to research it. Your warships get 20% more armour.

rows.desc: Blueprint. Put a Pop (slow) or a Scientist (fast) on it to research it. Your warships deal 15% more damage.

rows.name: Science Nexus
rows.desc: Blueprint. Put a Pop (slow) or a Scientist (fast) on it to research it. Then a Construction Ship + 20 Alloys + 10 Energy builds a Science Nexus: a flood of Research.

rows.name: Ring World

rows.name: Dyson Sphere

rows.name: Matter Decompressor

rows.name: Science Nexus

rows.name: Ring World

rows.name: Empire Corvette
rows.desc: A rival empire's corvette.

rows.name: Empire Destroyer

rows.desc: A rival empire's cruiser.

components.about: Ship components. Each row also makes a research technology (card tech_<id>: Scientist + research_inputs; inputs with keep=true are studied, not used up) and a Shipyard recipe (Shipyard + build_cost, once researched). Drop a component on a warship or starbase to fit it into a free slot. Damage goes to shields, then armor, then hull; vs_* multiply damage against each layer; pierce_* is the share that skips a layer. special: flak (cuts incoming explosive damage), arc (random damage). min_slots: the host needs at least this many slots.

rows.name: Red Laser
rows.desc: Energy weapon. Burns through armour, weak against shields.

rows.name: Blue Laser
rows.desc: Better laser. Study a Red Laser to discover it.

rows.name: UV Laser
rows.desc: Hotter laser between Blue and Gamma. Strong against armour.

rows.name: Gamma Laser
rows.desc: The finest laser. Study a Blue Laser with Exotic Gases.

rows.name: Plasma Cannon
rows.desc: Melts armour twice as fast as hull, but nearly useless against shields.

rows.name: Tachyon Lance
rows.desc: Huge spinal weapon. Battleships and Titans only.

rows.name: Arc Emitter

rows.desc: +15 shields, recharging 1 per second.

rows.name: Improved Deflector

rows.name: Dark Matter Deflector
rows.desc: +60 shields, recharging 4 per second.

rows.name: Psionic Shield
rows.desc: +40 shields that recharge very fast (7 per second).

rows.name: Nanocomposite Armor
rows.desc: +15 armour.

rows.name: Crystal-Infused Armor
rows.desc: +30 armour.

rows.name: Neutronium Armor
rows.desc: +55 armour.

rows.name: Dragonscale Armor
rows.desc: +50 armour that grows back (2 per second). Made with Living Metal from the Ether Drake's hoard.

rows.name: Regenerative Hull Tissue
rows.desc: Living hull: +5 hull and heals 1 hull per second, even in battle.

rows.name: Shield Capacitor
rows.desc: +5 shields and +2 shield recharge per second.

rows.name: Afterburners
rows.desc: +15% chance to dodge each shot.

recipes.about: Stacks that make something. A stack matches when its cards are exactly station + inputs (leaders whose boost_tag equals the recipe tag may ride along and speed it up). station may be a card id or tag:<tag>. time -1 means the station card's yield_time. Inputs with keep=true stay on the stack. outputs is a weighted table; "station.yield" means the station card's yield column. effect: none | open_board:random | open_board:guardian | set_flag:claimed. requires_system: any | claimed (the star system must be yours) | unclaimed. effect claim_system claims the system the stack is in. effect repair restores a damaged ship's hull and armour (only offered when it is damaged).

packs.about: Booster packs sold on every board. Drop Energy Credits on a pack to buy it. Each draw rolls the weighted contents table. unlock_moon/unlock_act gate when the pack appears.

rows.name: Exploration
rows.desc: Charts, curiosities, Envoys to meet other empires, and the odd amoeba.

rows.name: Industry
rows.desc: Raw materials and districts.

rows.name: Society
rows.desc: People, goods and the will to grow.

rows.name: Research
rows.desc: Research, blueprints, anomalies and the odd Scientist.

rows.name: Military
rows.desc: Alloys, admirals, ship parts, warship and weapon blueprints - and trouble.

rows.name: Frontier
rows.desc: New worlds, new ships, new enemies.

rows.name: Strategic Resources
rows.desc: The rare stuff Titans are made of.

loot.about: What a hostile card drops when destroyed. One row per hostile or boss card.

systems.about: Star systems. home opens at start (already claimed); guardian systems open in row order from Guardian Signals; surveying an Uncharted System (unlimited) rolls a random system: pick a row of kind random by weight, place its star cards, roll planets_min..planets_max planets from planet_pool, roll each extra by its chance, and give it a random name. A surveyed system must be claimed (recipe c_claim_system) before you can colonise, build outposts or work planets there; you can own at most rules.claim_limit systems.

rows.name: Capital System
rows.desc: Your capital. Your homeworld and starting cards are here.

rows.name: Yellow star system
rows.desc: An ordinary sun with a mix of worlds.

rows.name: Red dwarf system
rows.desc: Cold worlds around a dim star.

rows.name: Blue giant system
rows.desc: Scorched worlds under a giant star.

rows.name: Binary system
rows.desc: Two suns and plenty of worlds.

rows.name: Black hole
rows.desc: Almost nothing survives here, but the black hole itself gives Dark Matter.

rows.name: Neutron star
rows.desc: Crystal creatures feed on its radiation.

rows.name: Pulsar
rows.desc: Bathed in radiation. Great for science, bad for living.

rows.name: Asteroid belt
rows.desc: Rocks everywhere - and someone is already mining them.

rows.name: Nebula
rows.desc: A glowing cloud hiding gas giants and void creatures.

rows.name: Drake's Hoard
rows.desc: The Ether Drake sleeps over a perfect world.

rows.name: Rift of Echoes
rows.desc: Space folds wrong around this black hole.

rows.name: The Enigma
rows.desc: A fortress no one built, lit by a pulsar.

crises.about: Endgame crises. One is picked at random each run. The rift opens on the home board at rules.crisis_moon and spawns minions; the boss arrives rules.boss_delay_moons later (or as soon as the rift is destroyed).

rows.name: The Prethoryn Scourge
rows.warning: Swarms are pouring in from beyond the galaxy!
rows.desc: Extragalactic devourers.

rows.name: The Unbidden
rows.warning: A portal to another dimension has opened!
rows.desc: Extradimensional invaders.

rows.name: The Contingency
rows.warning: Ancient machines have woken to sterilise the galaxy!
rows.desc: A machine intelligence purging organic life.

species.about: Playable species, picked on the empire screen. Multipliers speed up work (1.25 = 25% faster) or scale Pop hull.

rows.name: Agrarian Mammalians
rows.desc: Born farmers. Food work 30% faster; Babies come 15% faster.

rows.name: Industrious Lithoids
rows.desc: Living rock. Mineral work 30% and Alloys 20% faster; tough Pops (+60% hull); Babies come 25% slower.

rows.name: Intelligent Avians
rows.desc: Quick minds. Research and blueprint research 30% faster, Energy 10%; frail Pops (-20% hull).

empires.about: Rival empires. Each run picks rules.empire_count of them. Strength = base + growth x moon^1.3 (x difficulty enemy strength).

rows.name: Tzynn Empire
rows.desc: Militarist slavers. Aggressive: they may declare war when they feel strong.

rows.name: Blorg Commonality
rows.desc: Friendly traders. Peaceful, with the best trade deals.

rows.name: Kingdom of Yondar
rows.desc: A devout monarchy. Balanced: fair trade, war only when provoked or much stronger.

rows.name: Iferyss Combine
rows.desc: A corporate republic. Balanced, rich in Alloys.

rows.name: Kel-Azaan Republic
rows.desc: Xenophobic isolationists. Aggressive and quick to grow.

tutorial.about: The first-run tutorial: a checklist shown in the corner of the table. Steps can be done in any order; the panel shows the first one not yet done. done_when: recipe:<id> (made at least once), made:<card> (a recipe produced it), has:<card> (one exists), has_tag:<tag>, flag:<pack_bought|opened_book|researched|traveled|fitted|admiral|battle_won|sold>, claimed:<n> (systems owned), act:<n>.

rows.text: Put a Pop to work on your Homeworld.
rows.hint: Your resources start at 0 (top bar). Drag a Pop (glowing) onto your Homeworld. A green bar fills, then Energy flies into the top bar.

rows.text: Put a Pop on the Agriculture District.
rows.hint: Everyone eats Food at the end of each moon (the first moon is free). Drag a Pop onto the Agriculture District.

rows.text: Put a Pop on the Mining District.
rows.hint: Minerals pay for buildings. Drag your last Pop onto the Mining District.
Once you have 4 Energy, click the Exploration pack on the right. Its cards land in the system you're looking at.
Press Tab. It lists everything you can make, with pictures. Press Tab or Esc to close it.
Click your Construction Ship and pick something to build (a Generator District helps pay Energy upkeep). The cost comes from your pool.
Blueprint cards (green) come from packs. Drag a Pop or a Scientist onto one. Research points come from a Research Lab or by studying a star.
Drag the Uncharted System card onto your Science Ship. A new system appears next to your capital.
Build a City District (Construction Ship), then put 2 Pops on it with 3 Food in your pool. The Baby grows into a Pop in 60 s.
Research Corvettes, then click your Shipyard and choose Corvette (2 Alloys). Alloys come from an Alloy Foundry worked by a Pop.
Build a weapon or shield at the Shipyard and drop it on a warship. Drop a better one later to swap it.
Drop your fleet on a monster. Compare your fleet's Strength with its Threat (shown above each card) first.

rows.text: Send a ship to another system.
rows.hint: Drag a stack that holds a ship into another system. The trip takes a few seconds.
In a system with no hostiles, stack your Construction Ship on its star with 2 Influence in your pool (Edict: click the Homeworld).
Research Colonization, order a Colony Ship at the Shipyard (add a Pop), then drop it on a habitable planet in a system you own.
Envoys come in Exploration packs. Stack an Envoy with your Science Ship: a rival empire's home system appears. Click its capital card.
Keep growing. Guardian Signals appear: survey them with a Science Ship to find guardians and their treasure.
